::: {#def-one-way-anova}
#### One-way analysis of variance

With the [mean squares](#def-mean-squares) of $k \ge 2$ groups
and $n > k$ observations in all,
the **one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA)** F-test of

$$
\begin{aligned}
  H_0: \mean_1 &= \mean_2 \\
  &= \cdots \\
  &= \mean_k
\end{aligned}
$$

against the alternative that at least two group means differ
uses the statistic

$$F \eqdef \frac{\text{MS}_\text{between}}{\text{MS}_\text{within}}.$$

Its p-value is $\Pr(F^* \ge F)$,
where $F^*$ has the $F_{k-1,\, n-k}$ distribution ([F-distribution](inference.qmd#def-f-dist)).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-f-statistic-size}
#### Interpreting the F statistic

Large values of $F$ mean that the group means are spread out
more than the variation within groups would explain.
For the groups of @exm-mean-squares,

$$
\begin{aligned}
  F &= 13.5 / 1 \\
  &= 13.5.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
